note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English; the alate is based only on a king and a queen, and the original states that the colour may be faded. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The smallest species of the genus, its known body length range overlapping that of A. retifaciens; the latter has large ocelli closely adjoining the compound eyes in the alate, very long hooked spines on enteric valve cushions 2, 3 and 4 of the worker, and the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible in a different position. The alate of A. tranquillus has the third spur of the fore tibia reduced, is larger, and has different proportions of the marginal teeth of the right mandible; its worker is also larger, with a more poorly developed enteric valve, especially on cushion 1. The alates of all the remaining species are larger: in A. muricatus the ocelli are farther from the compound eyes; in A. pectinatus, A. rastratus and A. sentosus the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible is longer than that of the second; in A. spinulatus the apical tooth is longer and the meso- and metanotum narrower. In the workers of the remaining species the middle of the swollen distal part of cushion 1 is not inflated and there is no second row of spines, the surface being flat or concave with scattered spines.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow; pilosity yellow, sparse. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.26–0.28. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/L1 0.53–0.58, Ra/Ri 0.71–0.74; in surface view the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 10.12–10.83; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin about half the length of that of the second marginal tooth, Ra/Ri·Rm 12.13–13.80. Fore tibia scarcely inflated, Ti/Tw 4.72–5.00; third apical spur almost reduced, about one quarter the length of the other two spurs. The midgut–hindgut junction is oblique; the enteric valve seat is sessile, attached to the second hindgut pouch, nearly dorsal in the unopened abdomen; cushion 1 is sclerotized along its whole length, half of it projecting beyond the tips of the spines of the other positions, the spines confined to the swollen distal end, the stalk smooth; the spines on the margin of the swollen end number 30–40, the middle of the broader part is inflated and bears a second row of long spines, behind which smaller spines are scattered; the cushions of the other positions bear 3–6 slender curved spines, evenly tapering, the tips almost straight, a few slightly hooked; no distinct minute spines were seen on the valve membrane outside or between the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brown, dark brown above the ocelli; fontanelle smaller than half the ocellus, roughly circular, its outline ill defined, flat or slightly concave, pale yellowish brown; central spot circular, flat or slightly raised, very small, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus pale brown, labrum yellow; frontal groove very indistinct, a flat yellowish brown crescent; antennae pale yellowish brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum pale brown, a dark transverse suture present; femora pale yellowish brown, tibiae paler, tarsi yellowish white. Abdominal tergites and dorsal spiracles pale yellowish brown, sternites and ventral spiracles very pale yellowish brown, the median part of the sternites paler; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule not very evenly rounded, slightly undulate; ocelli moderate, their distance from the compound eye from slightly more than half to five sixths of their minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly to moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.23–0.26, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture weakly developed. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.54–0.64, Ra/R4 0.69–0.84; in surface view the proximal end of the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 7.40–9.10; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, and its anterior margin is distinctly shorter than that of the second marginal tooth. Meso- and metanotum of moderate width at the constriction, M/W 0.28–0.31. Cephalic pilosity yellowish brown, the layer very even, outstanding setae very sparse, mostly in left–right pairs.
